rule: JS/TS conditional initializers and factory returns. A conditional `c ? a : b` is evidence when every branch is. A branch counts if it is a function literal, an alias of a function, a factory call, or such a conditional. A factory returns a function when a top-level `return` gives one of those, or a function declared in its body. A JSDoc `@type` comment is not evidence.
source: SPEC Decisions (2026-11-10, amendment): pdf.js calcRound, BrotliDecode
notes: calcRound: both branches are evidence (alias Math.fround; a call of the scanned factory makeRound, whose return is a conditional of functions). BrotliDecode: makeDecode returns decode, a function declared in its body; the JSDoc comment plays no part. notFn: makeValue returns 1, no evidence. mixed: one branch is notFn, a value with no evidence, so the conditional is no evidence. Arrow bindings are named functions, called high.
